data.description: One Artemis PRO server entitlement and four concurrent network developer sessions. Hardware, network adapters, hub and backup media sold separately. C IDE version 2 runs locally after network loading; shared source/results live on the server.
features: AIONix Server November 1981 services: users, groups, authentication, project permissions, home directories, quotas and administration
Repository: atomic multi-file commits, author/date/message, branches, release labels, diffs, rollback and comments tied to immutable revisions; isolated workspaces, saving is not committing
Collaboration: text channels, posts and replies with file/revision/commit references; shared calendar, meetings, invitations, tasks, owners, deadlines and milestones
C Development Environment 2: local Artemis ERA/Z80 builds; compact Aurelia/Aurelia+ TUI and local Z80 tools; queued server ERA/heavy builds
Initial targets CP/M/Z80 and AIONix/ERA with separate binaries, startup code and libraries; Breakthru TUI portability layer and target adapters
Reproducible builds record source revisions, compiler versions, build settings and target libraries
Network loader uses bounded transfers; acknowledged saves and recoverable workspaces after disconnect
Apple and Commodore target packages are future roadmap work; no launch support or binary compatibility claim

specification.server: Artemis PRO, recommended 1 MiB; existing 5 MB disk supports bounded pilot projects only. Archive old history and rotate external floppy backups; larger qualified storage required for substantial projects and is not bundled or priced here.
specification.clients: Artemis, Aurelia and Aurelia+ with network upgrade; Aurelia compact tools use sequential overlays within its CP/M memory profile. No full suite resident in 48 KiB claim.
specification.qualification: Four concurrent developers is a validation target, not measured throughput. Gate release on commit recovery, access control, backup/restore, conflict handling and both target regression suites.

commercial_unit.unit: one server, four concurrent developer sessions
commercial_unit.renewal: No automatic paid renewal assumed; first-year support capped at 12 staff-hours. Further work quoted separately.
commercial_unit.expansion: Additional concurrency packs planned, not priced or counted as shipping offers.

delivery_cost_assumptions.note: One combined package; do not add its client/server editions or old IDE/SDK to its cost. Development/NRE excluded from unit cost.

specification.sponsored_deployment: Autodesk whole-team deployment from late January 1982: team_development_program.json/autodesk_sponsored_deployment. Sponsor supplies hardware, qualified concurrency/storage and dedicated support beyond retail caps; retail entitlement remains unchanged.

adoption_pricing.reference_basis: Pre-change June 15 1982 Team Edition retail, previously used as the explicit November 1981 launch-price proxy. Not a historical market quotation.
adoption_pricing.scope: Launch and subsequent modelled snapshots through 1982; no change to June 1981 prelaunch availability. No automatic expiry or second compounded reduction.
adoption_pricing.rationale: User-authorized rapid-adoption price; explicit exception to balanced pricing and the cost floor. Preserve one server/four concurrent users, 20h onboarding, 12h first-year support, media and documentation. Hardware remains separate.
adoption_pricing.loss_treatment: Show actual negative unit contribution after dealer fees. Do not add the same shortfall a second time as a marketing expense in a future P&L. Forecast quantities and aggregate subsidy exposure require a separate demand review.
adoption_pricing.launch_cost_basis: Use the first costed June 1982 delivery snapshot as a disclosed proxy for November 1981; no fabricated November cost study.

data.name: AION Development System (Team / AIONix Server edition)

minimum_resources.status: Release profiling required; server recommended 1 MiB, clients use existing platform memory profiles and bounded overlays. No measured minimum asserted.

data.delivery: Included in Team Edition; network-loaded clients, local execution, shared server storage. Not a separate license.
data.support_status: November 1981 scenario offering, subject to documented qualification gates.
